title: Planning in India: From Five-Year Plans to NITI Aayog

questions.question: The Planning Commission was established on:
questions.rationale: It was created by a Government of India cabinet resolution on 15 March 1950 — not by statute — with the Prime Minister as chair; NITI Aayog replaced it via a resolution of 1 January 2015.

questions.question: The First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) was based on which model and gave top priority to:
questions.rationale: The First Plan followed the Harrod-Domar framework and targeted agriculture, irrigation, and power, achieving about 3.6% growth against a 2.1% target.

questions.question: The Second Five-Year Plan is identified with:
options: The Mahalanobis model and rapid heavy industrialisation
questions.rationale: P. C. Mahalanobis designed the Second Plan (1956-61) around heavy industry, reinforced by the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 and new steel plants at Bhilai, Rourkela, and Durgapur.

questions.question: The first 'plan holiday' (1966-69) was caused by:
options: Wars of 1962 and 1965 and two severe droughts
questions.rationale: The Third Plan collapsed under defence spending from the China and Pakistan wars plus the 1965-66 droughts; the plan lapsed into three Annual Plans and the rupee was devalued in 1966.

questions.question: The Rolling Plan concept (1978-80) was introduced by:
options: The Congress government under Indira Gandhi
questions.rationale: The Janata government terminated the Fifth Plan in 1978 and substituted a rolling plan revised every year — distinct from the 1966-69 and 1990-92 annual-plan interruptions.

questions.question: Which pairing of plan and theme is correct?
options: Fourth Plan — Garibi Hatao and self-reliance
Sixth Plan — direct attack on poverty (IRDP, NREP)
Eighth Plan — first plan after Independence
questions.rationale: The Sixth Plan (1980-85) institutionalised poverty programmes like IRDP and NREP; 'growth with stability' marked the Fourth Plan, and the Eighth was the first reform-era plan (1992-97).

questions.question: The last Five-Year Plan of India was the:
questions.rationale: The Twelfth Plan (2012-17), themed 'faster, more inclusive and sustainable growth', ended in 2017 without a successor because the Planning Commission had been dissolved.

questions.question: A key institutional difference between the Planning Commission and NITI Aayog is that NITI Aayog:
options: Is a think tank with no fund-allocation powers
Is chaired by the Finance Minister
questions.rationale: NITI Aayog distributes no plan grants — plan transfers gave way to Finance Commission devolution — and works through evidence, indices, and the Governing Council of Chief Ministers.

questions.question: NITI Aayog's National MPI reports multidimensional poverty falling from about 24.85% (2015-16) to:
questions.rationale: NITI Aayog's baseline report put National MPI poverty at 24.85% in 2015-16 and 14.96% in 2019-21 — about 13.5 crore people exiting multidimensional poverty.

questions.question: The Aspirational Districts Programme (2018) of NITI Aayog covers:
options: Districts with the highest per-capita income
questions.rationale: The programme monitors 112 lagging districts monthly on health, nutrition, education, and infrastructure, using competitive rankings to drive convergence.
